plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped pink-lilac flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The strap-like leaves appear the following spring and die back by summer. All parts are highly toxic due to colchicine.
plants.location: Native to Europe and North Africa meadows; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Colchicine from this plant is used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce polyploidy, doubling chromosome numbers in crops.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, bushy native perennial with masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers and narrow purple rays. It thrives in moist meadows and roadsides and is a crucial late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America; cultivated in gardens across temperate regions
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely heavily on New England asters for nectar to fuel their long autumn migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing clusters of tiny, intensely apricot-scented flowers in the leaf axils. It is a beloved ornamental across East Asia and is used to flavor teas, cakes, and liqueurs.
plants.location: Native to southern China and the Himalayas; grown in Japan, Korea, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: In China, the Mid-Autumn Festival is closely associated with osmanthus, and osmanthus cakes and wine are traditional treats.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub producing enormous, bowl-shaped flower heads composed of colorful bracts surrounding a central cluster of true flowers. It is adapted to nutrient-poor fynbos soils and fire cycles.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in Southern Hemisphere (September-November, with some flowering year-round)
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and its flower head can reach up to 30 cm across, the largest in the Protea genus.
